pageProps.title: Building LineageOS 14.1 for Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110)
pageProps.review: A step-by-step guide to setting up a LineageOS 14.1 custom ROM build environment, downloading source code, and preparing device-specific code to repurpose an old Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110) tablet.
pageProps.description: A guide to configuring a Docker build environment, syncing repositories, and compiling a custom ROM for the n5110
pageProps.content: ## Building LineageOS 14.1 for Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 (n5110) I have an old Samsung Galaxy Note 8.0 Wi-Fi (n5110) tablet lying around unused at home, so I decided to use it as a 'toy' for a project. While I haven't decided on a specific use case yet, I thought it would be good to use it as a device for `AOSP`-related builds and studies. I found remnants of an official build guide for the n5110 from LineageOS, the most famous AOSP-based custom ROM project, so I decided to try building it myself by referring to that. > **Reference:** [LineageOS Official Build Guide (n5100)] ### Prerequisites Before starting the build, you need to install the necessary system requirements and tools. - **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04 LTS or higher recommended - **RAM**: Minimum 16GB (32GB recommended) - **Disk Space**: At least 200GB of free space ### Install Build Packages To build Android, many dependency packages must be installed beforehand. However, in my experience, builds often fail due to tangled dependencies depending on the version of Ubuntu, Python, or various libraries being used. Therefore, it's much more convenient to create a dedicated Docker image for the build, completely isolating and controlling the build environment from the host. I'll configure the `Dockerfile` for the build in the environment setup section later in the build process. ### Initialize the LineageOS Source Repository Create a working directory and initialize the LineageOS source and n5110 device tree. ```sh { "title": "Initialize repo" } --- $ mkdir -p ~/android/lineage $ cd ~/android/lineage $ repo init -u https://github.com/LineageOS/android.git -b cm-14.1 --git-lfs --no-clone-bundle ``` ### Download the Source Code Now, download the source code using the `repo sync` command. The source code is very large, so it may take a long time depending on your network status. ```sh { "title": "Sync source code" } --- $ repo sync ``` ### Prepare Device Specific Code You need to prepare the kernel and vendor binaries for the n5110 device. ```sh { "title": "Extract proprietary blobs" } --- $ source build/envsetup.sh $ breakfast n5110 ``` However, perhaps because official support for the device ended long ago, I encountered an issue where the relevant code could not be correctly retrieved from the official LineageOS repository. ```sh { "title": "breakfast fail" } --- ... // [!code error] build/core/product_config.mk:254: *** _nic.PRODUCTS.[[device/samsung/n5110/lineage.mk]]: "vendor/samsung/smdk4412-common/smdk4412-common-vendor.mk" does not exist. Stop. // [!code error] build/core/product_config.mk:254: *** _nic.PRODUCTS.[[device/samsung/n5110/lineage.mk]]: "vendor/samsung/smdk4412-common/smdk4412-common-vendor.mk" does not exist. Stop. ``` After searching GitHub a bit more, I fortunately found an external repository (TheMuppets) that continuously backs up and supports vendor files for various old devices, including the n5110. To use this external repository, you need to add a manifest file in `.repo/local_manifests` to download the code and then manually link the paths. ```xml { "title": ".repo/local_manifests/vendor_samsung.xml" } --- // [!code highlight] // [!code word:vendor/samsung/proprietary_vendor_samsung] ``` After modifying the manifest, I performed `repo sync` again, connected the necessary directories with symlinks, and retried `breakfast`. ```sh { "title": "Setting path using symlink after code sync" } --- $ repo sync $ ln -s proprietary_vendor_samsung/smdk4412-common vendor/samsung/smdk4412-common $ breakfast n5110 ... // [!code error] build/core/product_config.mk:254: *** _nic.PRODUCTS.[[device/samsung/n5110/lineage.mk]]: "vendor/samsung/kona-common/kona-vendor.mk" does not exist. Stop. // [!code error] build/core/product_config.mk:254: *** _nic.PRODUCTS.[[device/samsung/n5110/lineage.mk]]: "vendor/samsung/kona-common/kona-vendor.mk" does not exist. Stop. ... ``` This time, an error occurs stating that files related to `kona-common` are missing. Fortunately, the `kona-common` directory was also included in the synchronized `proprietary_vendor_samsung` source, so I should be able to continue the build after adding another symbolic link. ```sh { "title": "Retry after adding symlink" } --- $ ln -s proprietary_vendor_samsung/kona-common vendor/samsung/kona-common $ breakfast n5110 ... // [!code error] build/core/product_config.mk:254: *** _nic.PRODUCTS.[[device/samsung/n5110/lineage.mk]]: "vendor/samsung/n5110/n5110-vendor.mk" does not exist. Stop. // [!code error] build/core/product_config.mk:254: *** _nic.PRODUCTS.[[device/samsung/n5110/lineage.mk]]: "vendor/samsung/n5110/n5110-vendor.mk" does not exist. Stop. ... ``` Next, an error occurred stating that `n5100`-related files were missing. Similarly, the `n5100` entry exists within the backed-up `proprietary_vendor_samsung` folder, so I'll create a symbolic link and try `breakfast` again. ```sh { "title": "Retry after adding symlink" } --- $ ln -s proprietary_vendor_samsung/n5110 vendor/samsung/n5110 -- breakfast n5110 including vendor/cm/vendorsetup.sh Looking for dependencies in device/samsung/n5110 Looking for dependencies in device/samsung/smdk4412-common Looking for dependencies in device/samsung/kona-common Dependencies file not found, bailing out. ============================================ PLATFORM_VERSION_CODENAME=REL PLATFORM_VERSION=7.1.2 LINEAGE_VERSION=14.1-20260306-UNOFFICIAL-n5110 TARGET_PRODUCT=lineage_n5110 TARGET_BUILD_VARIANT=userdebug TARGET_BUILD_TYPE=release ... ``` Finally, the `breakfast n5110` command completed successfully without any major issues. Now, let's start building the bootable ROM image in earnest. ### Start the Build As mentioned earlier, let's create a Docker image to perform the build consistently and without environment contamination. I've configured the `Dockerfile` as follows, including all essential build tools and packages listed in the official LineageOS documentation. ```docker { "title": "DockerFile" } --- FROM ubuntu:20.04 ARG USER_ID=1000 ARG GROUP_ID=1000 ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive ENV TZ=Asia/Seoul RUN apt-get update && \ apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends bc bison build-essential ccache \ curl flex g++-multilib gcc-multilib git git-lfs \ gnupg gperf imagemagick protobuf-compiler python3-protobuf \ lib32readline-dev lib32z1-dev libdw-dev libelf-dev \ libsdl1.2-dev libssl-dev libxml2 libxml2-utils lzop pngcrush \ rsync schedtool squashfs-tools xsltproc zip zlib1g-dev openssl unzip openjdk-8-jdk \ lib32ncurses5-dev libncurses5 libncurses5-dev \ python2 lz4 autoconf automake libtool gettext autopoint texinfo help2man indent texlive RUN update-alternatives --install /usr/bin/python python /usr/bin/python2 10 ARG USER_ID ARG GROUP_ID RUN if [ -n "$USER_ID" ] && [ -n "$GROUP_ID" ]; then \ addgroup --gid $GROUP_ID user && \ adduser --uid $USER_ID --gid $GROUP_ID --disabled-password --gecos '' user && \ adduser user sudo && \ echo '%sudo ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL' >> /etc/sudoers; \ fi ENV USE_HOST_LEX=yes ENV USE_HOST_BISON=yes WORKDIR /tmp RUN git clone https://github.com/westes/flex.git -b flex-2.5.39 && \ cd flex && \ ./autogen.sh && \ ./configure && \ make && \ make install RUN sed -i 's/TLSv1, TLSv1.1, //g' /etc/java-8-openjdk/security/java.security USER user ENV USER=user WORKDIR /lineage-n5110 CMD ["bash"] ``` Now, create the image via `docker build` and enter the container environment by volume-mounting the working directory where the Android source code is synchronized. Inside the container, set up the shell environment variables and then start the actual ROM build using the brunch command. ```sh { "title": "Build with docker" } --- $ docker build \ --build-arg USER_ID=$(id -u) \ --build-arg GROUP_ID=$(id -g) \ -t lineage-build-ubuntu20.04 . $ docker run -exec -it --rm -v `pwd`:/lineage-n5110 lineage-build-ubuntu20.04 /bin/bash # docker container user@d3c9f720c878:/lineage-n5110$ source build/envsetup.sh user@d3c9f720c878:/lineage-n5110$ brunch n5110 ... get/product/security/testkey.x509.pem build/target/product/security/testkey.pk8 /tmp/tmp26jaaU /lineage-n5110/out/target/product/n5110/lineage_n5110-ota-91ef8e8628.zip done. [100% 20581/20581] build bacon // [!code highlight] Package Complete: /lineage-n5110/out/target/product/n5110/lineage-14.1-20260306-UNOFFICIAL-n5110.zip make: Leaving directory '/lineage-n5110' #### make completed successfully (20:13 (mm:ss)) #### ``` Once the entire build process completes without errors, you can verify that the `lineage-*.zip` file for direct flashing and the `recovery.img` (recovery image) file have been successfully created in the `out/target/product/n5110/` directory. ```sh { "title": "Build result" } --- $ ls out/target/product/n5110 ... lineage-14.1-20260306-UNOFFICIAL-n5110.zip recovery.img ... ``` ### 4. Next Steps In this post, I've set up the environment and successfully completed the build of a LineageOS 14.1 custom ROM for the idle n5110 device. However, I haven't yet tested if the generated image works correctly on the actual tablet. In the next post, I'll flash the ROM file and recovery image I built using a Custom Recovery (e.g., TWRP) and check if it boots without any issues.
